key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin can rapidly screen in-space robotic welding settings and controller actions before costly flight-like experiments.
engineering_relevance: The framework de-risks metal joining for space assembly and repair by combining a thermal weld-pool model, surrogate models, and robot simulation to predict seam quality under constrained conditions.
method: Finite-volume thermal model with solid-liquid phase change, thermocapillary transport, and a local-pressure term.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates trained and validated with repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated six-axis UR5 welding study with a proportional controller adjusting power-source settings along an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: Across repeated five-fold cross-validation, the GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; in 10 held-out boundary cases, 74/80 solver responses fell within nominal 90% GP predictive intervals.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based and still need thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and hardware-in-the-loop testing to confirm real-world robustness.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
